chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from his father, from Uthman ibn Zayd, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you meets his brother, let him greet him and shake his hand, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, honored the angels with that, so do as the angels do.'

key_terms.أَخَاهُ: his brother (often used for fellow believers)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of shaking hands when greeting a fellow Muslim according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain to emphasize that the handshake is not merely a social courtesy but a spiritual act of emulation (*ittiba'*) of the angels, who are honored by this greeting. This practice reinforces the concept of *akhawah* (brotherhood) in Shia tradition, transforming a physical gesture into a means of attracting divine mercy and maintaining communal cohesion among the faithful.
